div.l: Wel outhe a prest ensaumple for to ȝeue
By hese clennesse how hese schep schulde leue
He sette not hese benefys to hyre
An let hese schep acumbrit in the myre
And ran to lundene vn to seynt poulys
To seke hym a chauntriye for soulys
Or with a broþerhed to be with holde
But dwelte at hom ⁊and kepte wel hese folde
So that þe wolf ne made it not myscarie
He was a schepherde ⁊and not a mersenarye
And þow he holy were ⁊and vertyuous
He was not to synful men dispitous
Ne of hese speche daungerous ne digne
But in hese techynge discreet ⁊and benygne
To drawyn folk to heuyn be clennesse
Be good ensaumple this was hese besynesse
But ȝif it were ony persone obstynat
What so he were of hey or low estat
Hym wolde he snybbyn scharpli for the nonys
A bettyr pryst I trowe neuere non is
He waytid aftyr no pompe ne reuerence
Ne makid him a spisede concience
But cristis lore ⁊and hese apostill twelue
He taughte but fyrst he folwede it hym selue
With hym þere was a plowman that was hese broþerA Plouman
That hadde led of donge manye a fodir
A trewe swynkere ⁊and a good was he
leuynge in pes ⁊and parfit charite
God louede he best with al hese hole herte
At alle tymys thow hym gamenede or smerte
And thanne his nyȝhe-bour riȝt as hym selue
He wolde throsche ⁊and þerto dyke ⁊ delue
For cristis sake for / euery pore wyght
With-outyn hyre / ȝif it leye in his myȝt
Hese tythis payede he ful fayre ⁊and wel
Bothe of propre swynk ⁊and his catel
